activitysource-sampling-listener.title: Understand ActivitySource sampling and listeners
activitysource-sampling-listener.short: Tracing work is controlled by listeners before an Activity is created
activitysource-sampling-listener.summary: ActivitySource is the .NET tracing entry point used by libraries and applications, while listeners decide which operations should be recorded and at what detail level.
activitysource-sampling-listener.why: Creating expensive tags before sampling decisions wastes work, while inconsistent source names and activity structure make distributed traces harder to use.
activitysource-sampling-listener.tips: Use stable source and operation names, defer expensive enrichment until an Activity is recorded, and keep high-cardinality data out of tags unless it is genuinely needed.

socketasynceventargs-buffer-ownership.title: Manage SocketAsyncEventArgs buffer ownership when pooling operations
socketasynceventargs-buffer-ownership.short: Reusable socket state needs explicit buffer and operation lifetimes
socketasynceventargs-buffer-ownership.summary: SocketAsyncEventArgs can retain reusable buffers and state across socket operations, so pooled designs must define when buffers may be replaced or returned.
socketasynceventargs-buffer-ownership.why: Returning or repurposing a buffer while an asynchronous socket operation still references it can corrupt data, while retaining buffers indefinitely wastes pooled memory.
socketasynceventargs-buffer-ownership.tips: Treat the active operation as the buffer owner, reset state only after completion, and prefer simpler Task-based socket APIs until measurement justifies pooling complexity.

memorymappedfile-view-lifetime.title: Manage memory-mapped view lifetime explicitly
memorymappedfile-view-lifetime.short: Mapped views own virtual-memory resources independently of ordinary buffers
memorymappedfile-view-lifetime.summary: MemoryMappedViewAccessor and related views expose regions of a MemoryMappedFile and should stay alive exactly while code accesses that mapped region.
memorymappedfile-view-lifetime.why: Keeping many views alive consumes address-space and mapping resources, while disposing a view before dependent access completes invalidates that access boundary.
memorymappedfile-view-lifetime.tips: Keep views narrowly scoped, separate map ownership from view ownership, and coordinate cross-process access explicitly when mappings are shared.

assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-resolu.title: Resolve managed and native dependencies for plugin load contexts
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-resolu.short: Use AssemblyDependencyResolver to follow a plugin's dependency graph
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-resolu.summary: AssemblyDependencyResolver maps assembly and unmanaged-library names to paths using a component's dependency metadata, making custom AssemblyLoadContext implementations more predictable.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-resolu.why: Searching arbitrary directories by filename can load the wrong version and makes plugin isolation fragile.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-resolu.tips: Create one resolver per plugin component, combine it with a dedicated AssemblyLoadContext, and define which assemblies are intentionally shared with the host.

aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.title: Apply endpoint filters to focused Minimal API concerns
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.short: Wrap endpoint execution without burying domain logic in handlers
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.summary: ASP.NET Core endpoint filters can perform validation, logging, transformation, or other endpoint-level work before and after a Minimal API handler.
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.why: Copying the same checks into every handler causes drift, while putting every concern into global middleware can lose endpoint-specific context.
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.tips: Keep filters small, order them deliberately, and use middleware or services instead when the concern belongs to the whole request pipeline or domain layer.

async-local-context-leak.title: Restore AsyncLocal context after a scoped operation
async-local-context-leak.short: Ambient async state can flow farther than intended
async-local-context-leak.summary: AsyncLocal<T> flows values through ExecutionContext across awaits, which is useful for request context but requires clear scope boundaries.
async-local-context-leak.why: Setting ambient state without restoring it can expose stale request or operation data to later work in the same logical execution flow.
async-local-context-leak.tips: Prefer explicit parameters for core data, scope ambient values with try/finally, and avoid storing large object graphs in AsyncLocal.

arraypool-return-sensitive-data.title: Clear sensitive pooled buffers before returning them
arraypool-return-sensitive-data.short: ArrayPool reuse means old bytes can be observed by later renters
arraypool-return-sensitive-data.summary: ArrayPool<T> improves reuse by retaining arrays, but returning a buffer does not guarantee that its previous contents are erased.
arraypool-return-sensitive-data.why: Secrets, credentials, or other sensitive bytes left in a shared pool can survive beyond the logical operation that owned them.
arraypool-return-sensitive-data.tips: Clear the used sensitive region before Return, track the actual used length, and do not assume clearArray is a substitute for carefully defining sensitive-data lifetime.

http-responsemessage-disposal-streaming.title: Keep HttpResponseMessage alive while streaming its content
http-responsemessage-disposal-streaming.short: Response and body lifetimes must cover the entire streaming read
http-responsemessage-disposal-streaming.summary: With ResponseHeadersRead, HttpClient returns after headers and the caller owns the response while the body is still being consumed.
http-responsemessage-disposal-streaming.why: Disposing the response too early interrupts streaming, while never disposing it can hold network resources longer than necessary.
http-responsemessage-disposal-streaming.tips: Use using for the response and await using for the content stream where appropriate, consume or cancel promptly, and propagate cancellation through the read loop.

cancellation-registration-lifetime.title: Bound CancellationToken registrations to their real lifetime
cancellation-registration-lifetime.short: Registrations retain callbacks and captured state until disposed or token cleanup
cancellation-registration-lifetime.summary: CancellationToken.Register creates a registration that may hold callback state for as long as the token source remains reachable.
cancellation-registration-lifetime.why: Long-lived tokens combined with short-lived operations can retain objects unnecessarily when registrations are never disposed.
cancellation-registration-lifetime.tips: Dispose registrations when the operation ends, keep callback captures small, and use cancellation-aware framework APIs instead of manual registration when available.

unity-profiler-marker-hot-path.title: Instrument Unity hot paths with reusable ProfilerMarker values
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path.short: Measure custom subsystems without creating profiling garbage every frame
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path.summary: ProfilerMarker adds named CPU samples that help separate application work inside Unity's Profiler timeline.
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path.why: Without focused markers, a large Update or job-scheduling region can hide which subsystem actually consumes frame time.
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path.tips: Store markers statically, mark meaningful regions rather than every tiny call, and profile representative player builds as well as the Editor.
